headline: Fitbit Edge leaks with 7-day battery, GPS, and altimeter
summary: Google's rumored fitness tracker appears to split the difference between the Pixel Watch and Fitbit Air, offering advanced features at a mid-range price.
details: Leaked images reveal Google's upcoming Fitbit Edge, a fitness tracker positioned to succeed the midrange Charge line. The device appears to blend design elements of the Pixel Watch and Fitbit Air, featuring a small screen capable of displaying widgets.

The Fitbit Edge is expected to offer a compelling fitness-first experience with a seven-day battery life, built-in GPS, and an altimeter. This would make it significantly more capable than the minimalist Fitbit Air.

Limited app support is anticipated, with mentions of Google Maps and YouTube Music. While specific details remain scarce, the Edge aims to bridge the gap between basic fitness trackers and full-fledged smartwatches.

The Fitbit Charge line's last update was in 2023, making a new midrange tracker timely. Although pricing and release dates are unconfirmed, industry speculation suggests a price point between $150 and $200, fitting between the $99.99 Air and the $399.99 Pixel Watch.

topic: app turns old pixel into bluetooth keyboard
headline_marked: [[Turn your old Pixel 4a]] into a Bluetooth keyboard and trackpad
headline: Turn your old Pixel 4a into a Bluetooth keyboard and trackpad
summary: An open-source Android app uses Bluetooth HID to transform spare phones into wireless input devices for PCs, consoles, and more, with customizable layouts and haptic feedback.
details: An old Google Pixel 4a can be repurposed into a wireless keyboard and trackpad using the Bluke app. This open-source solution leverages Android's native Bluetooth HID device profile, allowing users to control PCs, macOS, Linux, Chrome OS, and even gaming consoles without needing a companion app on the host device.

Bluke works completely offline and prioritizes user privacy by not tracking telemetry or serving ads. It exposes the device's HID profile, enabling seamless pairing and functionality. The app allows for customization of keyboard layouts, including 60%, 65%, and 75% styles, and offers various themes.

Beyond keyboard emulation, Bluke can also function as a trackpad or gamepad. While the gamepad mode is functional, it's not recommended for serious gaming. The app cleverly uses haptic feedback to simulate the tactile feel of mechanical keyboards, with options to emulate up to eight different switch types.

While Bluke won't replace a physical keyboard for extended typing sessions, it's a highly practical solution for media PCs, quick note-taking, or controlling devices like Android TVs. It supports multiple hosts, allowing users to switch between devices by simply reconnecting the Bluetooth connection.
